=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:lines ~3702-3713 within ensure_eager_final_pr | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The eager draft PR race fallback can still return an empty discovered value under concurrent poll cycles, so the caller may treat an existing PR as missing.
  WHY: Both reviewers report the fallback after `gh pr create --draft` can leave `discovered=""` when overlapping poll ticks race to create or find the same PR, breaking idempotent PR reuse.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:build_eager_pr_validation_status_block + update_eager_pr_validation_status_section (the regex + last_outcome fallback logic) | severity=medium | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: Validation-status derivation is duplicated across paths and can desync the PR-body status block from tracking-issue state when markers or outcomes change.
  WHY: x-ai reports the same marker stripping and outcome derivation logic across `/revalidate`, `finalize_integration_merge_if_needed`, and the eager-ahead sweep, so future marker or outcome changes can silently stale the PR body.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:_branch_head_sha, the REVALIDATE_INTEGRATION_SHA lookup in the /revalidate block, and the eager-ahead sweep that calls ensure_eager_final_pr | severity=medium | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: Branch SHA lookup and revalidate dedup rely on a single stale read and wall-clock window, so brief ref-propagation lag can cause duplicate revalidate events or miss the eager-PR creation race.
  WHY: x-ai reports the branch SHA is fetched once per poll cycle with no retry, and the 300 s actor+SHA dedup window can become non-idempotent under high poll load or transient GitHub lag.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:update_eager_pr_validation_status_section body update (Python heredoc) at ~5672-5714 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: The helper can return success even if the inline Python fails to update the PR body, leaving the validation section unchanged.
  WHY: A silent no-op can leave an outdated validation-status block visible while the poller believes the update was applied.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:lines ~3702-3713 within ensure_eager_final_pr | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The race-handler only calls gh pr list inside the else branch after gh pr create returns no URL, so numeric ahead cases can still leave discovered="" and PR-lookup empty.
  WHY: Concurrent poll cycles that both attempt creation can leave the first handler empty even if the second created, violating idempotency and potentially skipping PR reuse for a full cycle.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:lines ~3702-3713 within ensure_eager_final_pr via discovered path | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: discovered is returned empty when the first tick’s else branch wins and the PR already existed (created by concurrent), causing the caller to treat PR as missing and re-attempt or skip status refresh.
  WHY: Null or empty discovered breaks the caller and risks duplicate work or stale state skipping.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:update_eager_pr_validation_status_section body update (Python heredoc) at ~5672-5714 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: If the inline Python fails to mutate the PR body, the helper returns success (exit 0) instead of propagating the Python exit code, leaving the PR unchanged silently.
  WHY: A silent no-op can leave an outdated validation-status block visible while the poller believes the update was applied.
=== END FINDINGS FROM mistralai_mistral-small-2603 ===
